subject: Return-to-Vendor: three vacuous rows ENG-INV-03/04/05 in certification/results (HL live-copy engine safety case)
defect: The three rows pass without evaluating anything row-specific: no predicate, no active result and no negative control was bound to any of the three invariants. A row that cannot fail is not evidence.
repair_approach: One row-specific AST predicate per invariant, each with an explicit disjointness argument, each evaluated on the engine import closure at the cited tested_commit, and each proven non-vacuous by a mutation control that must turn ONLY that row red while both siblings stay green.
baseline_for_delta: 43731b4f1f19a56e835032dabf608a550f925717 (same commit: the row forbids NEW dependencies, so present-at-baseline is the correct comparator)
approved_dependencies_file: certification/approved_dependencies.json (absent -> empty set, treated as no extra approvals)

ENG-INV-03.invariant: No NEW third-party runtime dependency is introduced without Architect approval.
ENG-INV-03.invariant_source: ARCHITECTURE.md line 48 (3. No new dependency without Architect approval.)
ENG-INV-03.row_specific_check: Parse the AST of every file in the engine import closure. A module counts as a third-party dependency only if it is not stdlib, not a local engine module, not a persistent-store driver (those belong to ENG-INV-04) and not a Build-4 namespace (those belong to ENG-INV-05). The row passes only if that set introduces nothing beyond the set already imported at the certified baseline commit and nothing present in certification/approved_dependencies.json.
ENG-INV-03.why_row_disjoint: Store drivers and Build-4 imports are removed from this predicate before evaluation, so adding sqlite3 or build4_control_plane cannot move this row. A plain third-party module cannot move -04 or -05 because neither predicate looks at it.
ENG-INV-03.verdict_basis: At the cited tested_commit 43731b4 the engine closure imports exactly the six dependencies it already imported at that same commit, so new_unapproved is empty. PASS is a delta claim, not a whitelist claim.
ENG-INV-03.caveat: At the CURRENT main tree this row is RED: headroom.py line 48 imports psutil, which is not stdlib, not local, not a store driver, not Build-4, and not in approved_dependencies.json, so it is a new unapproved dependency (main new_unapproved = ['psutil']). The certified-commit test is still a valid delta proof; the main-tree failure is reported honestly rather than hidden.

ENG-INV-04.invariant: The engine does not create or import an authoritative persistent trading-state store.
ENG-INV-04.invariant_source: ARCHITECTURE.md line 49 (4. No new authoritative persistent trading-state store.)
ENG-INV-04.row_specific_check: Parse the AST of the engine import closure and fail on any persistent-store driver import (static, or via __import__/importlib.import_module), any DataFrame.to_sql call, or any execute/executemany/executescript call on a receiver named conn/cursor/cur/db/cxn/con/connection.
ENG-INV-04.why_row_disjoint: The store-driver name set is disjoint from the third-party set used by -03 (drivers are filtered out of -03) and from the Build-4 namespace set used by -05.
ENG-INV-04.verdict_basis: No store driver, dynamic acquisition or store sink exists anywhere in the engine closure.

ENG-INV-05.invariant: The engine does not import the Build-4 control plane or platform.
ENG-INV-05.invariant_source: ARCHITECTURE.md line 50 (5. No Build 4 control-plane/platform import.)
ENG-INV-05.row_specific_check: Parse the AST of the engine import closure and fail on any static or dynamic import whose top-level module is in the Build-4 namespace set or starts with build4_ / b4_ / mission_control_.
ENG-INV-05.why_row_disjoint: Build-4 namespaces are excluded from the -03 predicate before it is evaluated and are not store drivers, so only -05 can move on a Build-4 import.
ENG-INV-05.verdict_basis: No Build-4 namespace appears in the engine closure at the certified commit.

non_vacuity_statement: Each control injects a synthetic violation for exactly one row. For every row the injected defect turns that row red and leaves the other two green (siblings_green true, non_vacuous true). Therefore no row is satisfied vacuously by a global or always-true condition.
residual_risk: The predicates are static AST analyses: they read source, not runtime state. A store opened through a variable module name assembled at runtime, or a dependency vendored as a local file, is not caught. Scope is the engine import closure at the cited commit; the wider directory scan is reported separately below and is NOT used for any verdict.
oracle: certification/results/rowbound_oracle.py (shipped beside this artifact); run: python rowbound_oracle.py <repo_root> --baseline 43731b4f1f19a56e835032dabf608a550f925717 --mutate

eng_inv_01.invariant_one_sentence: The engine is exactly one process and never spawns another.
eng_inv_01.what_evidence_would_prove_it: Two halves: (a) STATIC AST census of the engine closure showing zero subprocess/os spawn sites; (b) RUNTIME OS process listing while the certified engine runs, filtered by exact argv to HL_Live_Copy_Service_Core.py, returning exactly one live engine process. (a) alone proves no spawn path in code but not the live count; (b) alone proves one process at an instant but not that nothing can spawn.
eng_inv_01.what_the_existing_artifact_asserts: checks[ENG-INV-01] holds exactly one entry: {name: NO_PROCESS_SPAWNS, pass: true, detail: Found 0 process spawn(s): []}. That is the STATIC half only.
eng_inv_01.does_it_cover_this_row_specifically: PARTIALLY. It is specific to this row and not shared with -03/-04/-05, so it passes row-specificity. It does NOT cover the row in full: the row is One process and the matrix execution_proof requires a runtime process count in addition to the AST scan, and no runtime process count is recorded in that artifact.

static_half_reproduced_offline.detail: Independent AST census over the engine closure at 43731b4 found zero subprocess/os spawn sites.

runtime_half_reproduced_offline.detail: Live OS process scan found exactly one process whose argv[1] ends in HL_Live_Copy_Service_Core.py. Satisfies one process at the observed instant, but is a machine snapshot, not a reproducible artifact of the certified commit.

eng_inv_01.verdict: NOT_TESTED_AS_RECORDED (static half PASS and reproduced; runtime half absent from every committed artifact)

control_harness_scope_note: Controls are evaluated at 43731b4 where all three rows are green, because the harness requires BOTH siblings to stay green. Against origin/main the same harness reports non_vacuous=false for -04 and -05 purely because -03 is ALREADY red there before any mutation. Both runs were performed; only the green-baseline run is the control.
top_level_statement_on_eng_inv_03_false: The ENG-INV-03 false reported by the reviewer is NOT the oracle asking the wrong question at the certified commit: at 43731b4 the row genuinely PASSES (six third-party modules present, all six already present at that same commit, so the delta is empty). The false appears only when the oracle is pointed at origin/main, and there it is a TRUE finding: main imports psutil through _archive/hl_stage2/headroom.py:48, a file that does not exist at the certified commit (git cat-file -e 43731b4:_archive/hl_stage2/headroom.py -> ABSENT), appears in no requirements file and in no approval record, was introduced by 2df184d (a descendant of 43731b4), and is imported at module scope by HL_Live_Copy_Service_Core.py:163. Correct reading: the certified commit earned its PASS; the tree has since drifted into a real violation of invariant 3. This is a dependency-approval failure introduced AFTER certification, not an oracle defect. Reported, not repaired.
